set.body:
Recorded so the question is not reopened without new information.

A macro-checked formula DSL was considered and declined:

1. The typed path ALREADY EXISTS. ModelFormula is a public, directly constructible AST and EventModelBuilder.buildEither accepts it with no string involved. A macro would add a THIRD front-end duplicating FormulaParser, not remove a string.
2. It would improve the errors that are already good. Measured: all 7 formula-shape mistakes already return FormulaParse(detail, pos) with a character offset. Moving that to compile time is real but incremental.
3. It cannot touch the errors that are bad. The 4 mistakes that degrade to BuildFailed are SEMANTIC — unknown column, list/HRF column used as a factor, unknown basis call — and depend on a DataTable not known at compile time.
4. There is nothing to check yet: zero string-literal formulas exist outside tests, so today the only beneficiary would be the test suite.
5. Cost is non-trivial: FormulaParser would have to move to a module compiled before its use site, plus a macro module, on a cross-compiled JVM/JS build containing no macros today.

A schema-typed DataTable (Scala 3.7 named tuples) WOULD catch the semantic errors a macro cannot. Also declined: it collides with the data source. bids4s is wired in and a BIDS events.tsv is read at RUNTIME, so a compile-time schema needs an unchecked escape hatch for the dominant case — taxing every user for a guarantee the common path cannot have.

Conditions that would make this worth reopening:
- a user-facing scripting layer appears and literal formulas become common (the parser is self-contained, so the module split stays cheap)
- a compile-time-known schema becomes the normal case rather than the exception

Proportionate alternative already captured as phase 5 of the plan: col"..." / term"..." interpolators that validate a single identifier at compile time. No parser needed at compile time, so no module split, and they compose with the direct-AST path.

Context: docs/plans/design-hardening.md section 5.
set.title: DECISION: no formula macro; no schema-typed DataTable
